question: The strategic warfare manager: swm_window and swm_list_entry, what it measures from which lists and how it is drawn.

structs.name: CStratWarfareWindow
structs.comment: The strategic warfare manager window. Slots: 0 Build, 1 scalar deleting destructor, 2 Show, 3 Hide, 4 IsVisible, 5 Update. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
structs.evidence: operator new 0x17C before the sole call to the constructor (0x6CC786); vftable written at 0x466102; RTTI.

structs.name: CCountryEntry
structs.comment: A row of the manager's `listbox_countries`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
structs.evidence: operator new 0x88 in the rebuild (0x467E21); RTTI for the class name; the fields read in the constructor.

structs.name: StrategicWarfareRecord
structs.comment: One enemy the played country has been at war with: three categories (naval, air, land), each three rings. The game state's strategic_warfare keeps one per enemy. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
structs.evidence: operator new 0x24 in GameStrategicWarfare_CreateRecord at 0x463210; written by StrategicWarfareRecord_Init; agrees with every top-level strategic_warfare block saved.

structs.name: StrategicWarfareRing
structs.comment: A ring of 0x40-byte, eight-column Fixed15 elements: the save's `container` blocks. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
structs.evidence: operator new 0x20 three times in StrategicWarfareRecord_Init; saved fields of StrategicWarfareRing_SaveContents.

structs.name: GameStrategicWarfare
structs.comment: The game state's strategic warfare record (+0xD68): the played country's tag and a std::map of enemy records. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
structs.evidence: GameStrategicWarfare_SaveContents and GameStrategicWarfare_DailyUpdate read it this way; the key `strategic_warfare` of the save.

addresses.name: CStratWarfareWindow::CStratWarfareWindow
addresses.signature: CStratWarfareWindow* __stdcall CStratWarfareWindow::CStratWarfareWindow(CStratWarfareWindow* this, void* gui, void* screen)
addresses.comment: The strategic warfare manager window, 0x17C bytes, one per top bar (CTopBar +0x380, made in CTopBar::Build at 0x6CC7BA). Sets every button glue, then calls slot 0 (CStratWarfareWindow::Build) once. Six glues (CButtonObserverGlue<CStratWarfareWindow>): close +0x58, tabs +0x84, select_all +0xB0, select_present +0xDC, select_none +0x108, duration buttons +0x134. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: `ret 0xC` at 0x4662FA; vftable 0x15BD104 written at 0x466102; the string swm_window at 0x466086; size from operator new 0x17C at 0x6CC786 just before the call at 0x6CC7BA.

addresses.name: CStratWarfareWindow::ScalarDeletingDestructor
addresses.comment: Slot 1. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Slot 1 of the table at VA 0x15BD104; `ret 4` at 0x46631F; calls the destructor at 0x466330 and frees on bit 0.

addresses.name: CStratWarfareWindow::~CStratWarfareWindow
addresses.comment: Tears the window object down: destroys the gui window (+0x24, its slot 20), frees the shown-tags vector +0x160 and resets the glues. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: `ret 4` at 0x4663FC; writes the vftable at 0x46634E; RTTI names it the destructor.

addresses.name: CStratWarfareWindow::Build
addresses.comment: Slot 0, run once by the constructor (and whenever the gui is rebuilt): (re)creates `swm_window`, finds tab_naval, tab_air, tab_land with sub_naval, sub_air, sub_land and tags each tab with its index through slot 0xD4; the sub windows start hidden; finds listbox_countries, select_all, select_present, select_none, close_button; finds duration_1..duration_3, tags each with its index; passes the string "topbar" to slot 0x78 of the gui window's interface at +0x18 (what that does was not read); sets duration 0 and all tab frames (tab selected 2, others 1; duration selected 1, others 2), and redraws. Tab starts at 0 (naval), duration at 0. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Bare `ret` at 0x466CCD and 0x466C9A; slot 0 of the RTTI vftable 0x15BD104; the strings are each pushed here. Which of the frame numbers is the art is read from the code, not the textures.

addresses.name: CStratWarfareWindow::Show
addresses.comment: Slot 2. Shows the window (its slot 0x34), syncs the tab pages, and the first time ever (byte +0x178) selects the present rows; if it was hidden, slot 5 with force. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Slot 2 of the table at VA 0x15BD104; bare `ret` at 0x466D16.

addresses.name: CStratWarfareWindow::Hide
addresses.comment: Slot 3: the close button and the toggling swm_open both end here. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Slot 3 of the table at VA 0x15BD104; tail-jump through the window slot 0x38 (Hide) at 0x466D32.

addresses.name: CStratWarfareWindow::IsVisible
addresses.comment: Slot 4: the window object is present and its +0x5B visible byte set. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Slot 4 of the table at VA 0x15BD104; reads window +0x5B.

addresses.name: CStratWarfareWindow::Update
addresses.comment: Slot 5, called every frame by CTopBar::Update while the window is shown (force 0) and by Show with force 1: rebuilds the list when the game record changed (RebuildCountryList), then the listbox's slot 31; redraws (Refresh) when the hour of the day differs from the last draw, or force. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Slot 5 of the table at VA 0x15BD104; `ret 4` at 0x466E4D; tick +0x174 compared at the (tick - 43800000) % 24 test; called at 0x6C9FE9 with 0.
addresses.revises: was CStratWarfareWindow::GetTabTooltip, recorded mainly for its boundary with the wrong name; it builds no tooltip: it is the window's per-frame update (rebuild and hourly refresh)

addresses.name: BuildStratWarfareTooltip
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __stdcall BuildStratWarfareTooltip(CStratWarfareWindow* window, Hoi3CString* out, CGuiObject* element)
addresses.comment: The manager's tooltips: element is the element under the mouse (CTopBar::BuildTooltip passes it). tab_naval/tab_air/tab_land give SWM_TOOLTIP_TAB_NAVAL/_AIR/_LAND; a chart of the shown tab (found by name through the sub window +0x48[tab], slot 0x44) gives its SWM_TOOLTIP_* line, 16 charts by name in three arms; any other element inside the window answers an empty tooltip, and CTopBar::BuildTooltip returns straight after this call so a shown window's elements never reach the bar's own tooltips. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: `ret 0xC` at 0x467C3D; decompiled whole. Caller 0x6CCBED gates on CStratWarfareWindow::IsVisible and the window slot 0x94 (element inside the window).
addresses.revises: comment only: says what the third parameter is (an element, not a mode), and which elements answer

addresses.name: CStratWarfareWindow::OnTabClicked
addresses.comment: Glue +0x84 handler: the button's stored index (slot 0x80) becomes the tab (+0x20), then SyncTabs and Refresh. A click on the tab already open still redraws. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: `ret 4` at 0x466424; the handler the constructor stores at +0xA4.

addresses.name: CStratWarfareWindow::SetDuration
addresses.comment: Stores the duration (+0x170: 0 month, 1 year, 2 conflict), gives duration_N frame 1 for the chosen and 2 for the others, and redraws. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: `ret 8` at 0x466472; called from OnDurationClicked and the constructor's default.

addresses.name: CStratWarfareWindow::OnDurationClicked
addresses.comment: Glue +0x134 handler; the button's stored index passes to SetDuration. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.

addresses.name: CStratWarfareWindow::OnSelectAll
addresses.comment: select_all: every row not selected becomes selected and its two checkboxes are ticked; then Refresh. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Bare `ret`; ctor handler at +0xB8. Row selection is the generic list item byte +0x18 (0xA7F7B0).

addresses.name: CStratWarfareWindow::OnSelectPresent
addresses.comment: select_present: rows whose war is running (record +0x1C clear) are selected and ticked; rows whose war has ended are unselected and unticked; then Refresh. Also what Show runs the first time the window opens. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Bare `ret` at 0x466611; reads the record through row +0x28.

addresses.name: CStratWarfareWindow::OnSelectNone
addresses.comment: select_none: every selected row is unselected and unticked; then Refresh. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.

addresses.name: CStratWarfareWindow::SyncTabs
addresses.comment: For each tab: frame 2 for the current tab, 1 otherwise; the current sub window shown (slot 0x34), the others hidden (slot 0x38). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.

addresses.name: CStratWarfareWindow::RebuildCountryList
addresses.comment: Rebuilds listbox_countries when the game state record's map (+0xD68 +8) no longer matches the +0x160 vector of ids, or the record's dirty byte +0x18 is set (which it clears). Remembers the selected rows by country id, destroys the rows, makes one CCountryEntry per record with a value (std::sort in the record map's order, the running wars first: a record sorts before another only when it is running and the other ended, ties keep map order), adds them, and reselects by id. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: `ret 4` at 0x4680AD; decompiled whole; comparator read from the insertion sort at 0x46C190 (the two `+0x1C` byte tests).

addresses.name: CStratWarfareWindow::Refresh
addresses.comment: Draws what the current tab and duration show from the selected rows: for each pair of charts two series vectors (GatherSeries), the larger of 0.01 and every value is the common chart maximum, each chart gets its country-coloured lines (SetChartSeries), the max text, the totals text and the comparator frame. Which series is which chart is in the write-up. The whole of the window's content. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: `ret 4` at 0x46B413; series indices, categories and text keys each read from the listing, not the decompiler (the decompiler aliases the stack).

addresses.name: CStratWarfareWindow::GatherSeries
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CStratWarfareWindow::GatherSeries(CStratWarfareWindow* this, void* out, void* selected, int series, int category)
addresses.comment: Per selected country id: a series entry {values of series `series` of category `category` from the current duration ring, newest first, zero padded to the ring's size; the country colour}. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: `ret 0x14` at 0x4685AB; arguments pushed `category, series, selected, out, window` at each call site; duration read from +0x170.

addresses.name: StratWarfare_SetChartSeries
addresses.signature: void __stdcall StratWarfare_SetChartSeries(void* chart, void* series, unsigned int maxLow, unsigned int maxHigh)
addresses.comment: Turns series vectors into a line chart's points: each value v becomes point height = (v * 32768 / max) * 100 in whole percent (shifted down by 30, so the height is whole hundredths), point order reversed so the newest is last, colour the series'; with no series one three-point line of height 0 in the CColor {0x18D, 0, 1, 0, 1} (the default). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.

addresses.name: StratWarfare_SetSubwindowChart
addresses.signature: void __stdcall StratWarfare_SetSubwindowChart(void* subwindow@ECX, void* series@stack:4, void* name@stack:8, unsigned int maxLow@stack:0xC, unsigned int maxHigh@stack:0x10)
addresses.comment: Finds a chart by name in a sub window (slot 0x44) and calls StratWarfare_SetChartSeries on its drawn object at +0x88. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.

addresses.name: CStratWarfareWindow::SumSeriesTotal
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CStratWarfareWindow::SumSeriesTotal(void* selected@EDI, CStratWarfareWindow* this@stack:4, __int64* out@stack:8, int series@stack:0xC)

addresses.evidence: `ret 0xC` at 0x4686FD; EDI list seen at the call site 0x46939F; the category is +4 of the record at 0x4686AB.

addresses.name: StratWarfare_SeriesMax
addresses.signature: void __stdcall StratWarfare_SeriesMax(void* seriesList@EAX, __int64* out@stack:4, unsigned int floorLow@stack:8, unsigned int floorHigh@stack:0xC)
addresses.comment: The largest signed 64-bit Fixed15 value in the series vectors, starting from the floor passed. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.

addresses.name: StratWarfare_SeriesTotal
addresses.signature: unsigned int* __fastcall StratWarfare_SeriesTotal(__int64* out@ECX, void* seriesList@EAX) @EAX
addresses.comment: The sum of every value of the series vectors. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.

addresses.name: StrategicWarfare_ListMatchesRecords
addresses.comment: Whether the id vector +0x160 is exactly the record map's keys with a value, in map order. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.

addresses.name: CCountryEntry::CCountryEntry
addresses.signature: CCountryEntry* __stdcall CCountryEntry::CCountryEntry(void* gui@ECX, CCountryEntry* this@stack:4, void* parent@stack:8, void* record@stack:0xC, void* window@stack:0x10) @EAX
addresses.comment: A row of `listbox_countries`: window `swm_list_entry`, the record of an enemy and the owning window. background_button_present is shown for a running war and background_button_past for an ended one (never both); the row's country text is the enemy's name, country_flag is the enemy's flag, color_icon gets the enemy's country colour, date_begin and date_end via CCountryEntry::SetDates. 0x88 bytes. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: `ret 0x10` at 0x465AE3; operator new 0x88 at 0x467E21; RTTI names the class.

addresses.name: CCountryEntry::ScalarDeletingDestructor
addresses.comment: Slot 0. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Slot 0 of the RTTI table; `ret 4` at 0x465B72.

addresses.name: CCountryEntry::OnChecked

addresses.evidence: Bare `ret` at 0x465F90; ctor stores it at +0x58.

addresses.name: CCountryEntry::OnUnchecked

addresses.evidence: Bare `ret` at 0x465F4B; ctor stores it at +0x60.

addresses.name: CCountryEntry::SetSelected

addresses.evidence: Slot 7 of the RTTI table; `ret 4` at 0x465FFA.

addresses.name: GameStrategicWarfare_Clear
addresses.comment: Frees every record and each category's three rings, and empties the map. Named in CGameState::ResetSession's comment as 0x462D60. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.

addresses.name: GameStrategicWarfare_ResetIfPlayerChanged
addresses.no_signature: The record arrives in EDI, no parameters otherwise.
addresses.comment: At CInGameIdler's per-frame call when the played country id differs from the record's: Clear, SetUpForNewGame with the state's player, and the dirty byte +0x18. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Bare `ret`; EDI = the record at the sole site 0x655AC6.

addresses.name: GameStrategicWarfare_DailyUpdate
addresses.comment: Called first in RunDailyPass. Per record in map order: if running, AdvanceDay, and if the two countries are no longer at war (the played country's diplomacy status [enemy id]->War is null) it is marked ended (+0x1C = 1, end_tick = tick). If ended and at war again: the three categories are zeroed, start_tick = tick, running again. Then every country the player is at war with (CCountry CurrentAtWarWith) with no record gets a new one. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: `ret 4` at 0x463209; called at 0x682C64 in RunDailyPass; decompiled whole.

addresses.name: GameStrategicWarfare_CreateRecord
addresses.comment: A new record (0x24 bytes) for `enemy`: start_tick = *tick, running, years = whole years from the start to the defines' end_date + 1, and its nine rings. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: `ret 4` at 0x4632D9; decompiled whole; years = (int)(start / -365.0) - (int)(end / -365.0) + 1 with day counts.

addresses.name: StrategicWarfareRecord_Init
addresses.signature: void __stdcall StrategicWarfareRecord_Init(void* record, unsigned int years)
addresses.comment: Stores years and makes three categories (naval, air, land), each a ring of 30 days, 12 months and `years` years of 0x40-byte, eight-value elements; the day ring starts with offset 1. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: `ret 8` at 0x462257; decompiled whole; matches every save block.

addresses.name: StrategicWarfareRecord_AdvanceDay
addresses.comment: Daily, per category. Day ring: offset advanced with wrap, the slot now at `offset` zeroed. Unless the day ring has just wrapped to 0, the month element is the sum of the day ring (with the current slot) and the year element the sum of the month ring; on a wrap the month element is summed without the slot, the month ring advances; on the month ring wrapping likewise the year ring advances. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: `ret 4` at 0x462421; decompiled whole; agrees with the rings of two saves.

addresses.name: StrategicWarfareRecord_CurrentElement
addresses.comment: The day ring element a tally adds to: at offset - 1 (ring order), 0 where the ring is empty. So events land in the previous slot, the slot at offset stays empty until the next day. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.

addresses.name: StrategicWarfareRecord_GetCountryColour
addresses.comment: The enemy country's CColor (CCountry +0xC34..+0xC48, the map colour). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Bare `ret`; FUN_4CCCC0 copies the colour fields.

addresses.name: GameStrategicWarfare_HasRecord
addresses.comment: Whether a record exists for that country. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.

addresses.name: GameStrategicWarfare_RecordBombingEnd
addresses.comment: From CBomberCombatant::ReportBombingEnd, for a bombing the played country is a side of: whether the player bombed or was bombed decides the argument order to TallyBombing. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.

addresses.name: GameStrategicWarfare_TallyBombing
addresses.signature: int __stdcall GameStrategicWarfare_TallyBombing(void* warfare, void* combatant, void* bomberTag, void* targetTag)
addresses.comment: Air category's four columns of an ended bombing, added to the day element of the enemy's record: slot 0/4 the bombers' lost value (the bomber IC of `CalculateUnitDamageIC`), 1/5 the IC cost of the damaged buildings and the destroyed goods (goods at RESOURCE_TO_IC_COST), 2/6 the bomber strength lost, 3/7 the buildings' raw damage. Slots 4-7 where the played country is the bomber. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: `ret 0x10` at 0x46445D; decompiled whole; series use agrees with the Update arms and with the saves' air columns.

addresses.name: GameStrategicWarfare_TallyConvoyRaid
addresses.no_signature: Register-convention: EAX, ECX and EDX all carry state from the call site at 0x5D2670 and seven stack words.
addresses.comment: From ResolveConvoyRaid: for the played country as raider or victim, adds to the naval category's day element the raid's three figures: 0/3 convoy IC lost (StratWarfare_ConvoyLossIC), 1/4 cargo tons lost (StratWarfare_CargoTonsSunk), 2/5 the raiding navy's damage value (StratWarfare_UnitDamageIC of the raider, flags navy). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.

addresses.name: StratWarfare_ConvoyLossIC
addresses.no_signature: cdecl arguments plus register inputs EAX (tag) and ESI (out).
addresses.comment: Convoy IC lost: (escort build time * build cost) / CONVOY_CONSTRUCTION_SIZE times ships lost, plus for transports the transport build-cost term; Fixed15. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.

addresses.name: StratWarfare_CargoTonsSunk
addresses.signature: unsigned int* __cdecl StratWarfare_CargoTonsSunk(unsigned int* out, unsigned int shipsLost, unsigned int ships, int convoy)
addresses.comment: Sum of the convoy's seven goods (convoy +8..+0x20) x the defines' CARGO_TONS_SUNK_SCALE x the fraction of the convoy lost. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.

addresses.name: StratWarfare_UnitDamageIC
addresses.no_signature: cdecl-shaped with register inputs: EDI an out pointer (the 8 byte result).
addresses.comment: The value of a unit's losses in Fixed15: walks every sub-unit type with the flags (ships/regiments/bombers) asked for; strength lost (0..1000) x the type's full build cost for a sub-unit fully lost, or the reinforcement fraction for damage. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.

addresses.name: StratWarfare_SubUnitPartialCost
addresses.no_signature: Register input EAX (the country), EDX (out) and cdecl stack.
addresses.comment: The IC (and manpower) of a part of a sub-unit: reinforcement cost for strength lost: IC term (sub-unit Fixed15 lost / base) * build_cost * build time scale, manpower term likewise. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.

addresses.name: GameStrategicWarfare_AddToSeriesZeroOrFour
addresses.no_signature: Called with ECX=record, EAX/EDX=side, three stack words.
addresses.comment: Adds an amount to slot 0 of the record (or 4 for the player's own bombers) in the air category. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.

addresses.name: GameStrategicWarfare_RecordBomberLosses
addresses.no_signature: ECX record, EAX the combat, one stack word.
addresses.comment: Air combat end: a tally of the bombers each side lost (raw strength) added through GameStrategicWarfare_AddToSeriesZeroOrFour; for the side the played country is on. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C.

addresses.name: GameStrategicWarfare_TallyLandDamage

addresses.name: GameStrategicWarfare_SaveContents
addresses.no_signature: thiscall-shaped - the object in ECX, the writer on the stack, `ret 4` - but the object's class is not established, so no Class::Method signature can be written; it would be `void __thiscall ?::SaveContents(void* this, CSaveWriter* writer)`.
addresses.comment: **The top-level `strategic_warfare` block**, called directly (not through a vftable) by CGameState::SaveContents on the object at [state +0xD68]: `player` (the tag string at the object's +0), `count` (how many nodes of the std::map whose header is at +0xC hold a value at node +0x10), then each such value through rva 0x626F0, which writes `<its name at +0xC> = { end=yes/no start_date=.. end_date=.. (only when ended) years=N <three sub-lists> }`. Most of the maintainer's saves have `count=0`, but two do not (Germany1936_03_31_19: 8 enemies, Germany1936_09_02_21: 7), and those carry whole rings. The object and its entries were read for the strategic warfare manager: one per enemy the played country has been at war with, see reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topscreens.md, section C. `ret 4` at 0x4654C6. The name is ours.
